newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: France's Chirac hails Kohl's "determined action".
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac hails Kohl's "determined action".

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac hailed Chancellor Helmut Kohl's "determined action" on Thursday and said he looked forward to continuing to build a united Europe with him.

In a "Dear Helmut" birthday message to the German leader, released by French officials while he was visiting Prague, Chirac did not refer specifically to Kohl's announcement on Thursday that he intended to seek re-election next year.

But he publicly voiced admiration for the chancellor on the day Kohl ended months of uncertainty by telling German television on his 67th birthday that he planned to seek an unprecedented fifth term of office in 1998.
"May the coming year bring you health, personal happiness and full success in your determined action at the head of the German government and in all your endeavours," Chirac wrote.
"It is a great pleasure for me to work with you for progress in Franco-German cooperation, which we both want to make ever stronger, particularly to continue the construction of Europe."
Chirac said he looked forward to meeting Kohl in a few days' time in Bonn to prepare for this year's major summits on European Union reform and NATO reform.
No date has been announced for the meeting, but the two leaders hold informal dinners roughly every six weeks to confer on European and bilateral issues.
French officials said Kohl's announcement came as little surprise, since Chirac had always assumed the Christian Democratic chancellor, in office since 1982, would stand again.

Officials close to the president say they consider Kohl the strongest guarantor of the planned single European currency and see his determination to seek reelection as a clear sign that the project will go ahead on time in January 1999.
"Kohl has always said that completing European monetary and political unification is the second part of his life's work following German unification," one senior French official said.
